findings.title: Wire the new timeout setting into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: With no environment override, shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but the runtime timeout remains 60.0 (confirmed locally). scheduler.py:70–81 reads only the environment at import time, and line 634 uses that constant. Operators extending the drain through TOML will still have resources forcibly closed after 60 seconds while a search remains active.
findings.why_it_matters: With no environment override, shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but the runtime timeout remains 60.0 (confirmed locally). scheduler.py:70–81 reads only the environment at import time, and line 634 uses that constant. Operators extending the drain through TOML will still have resources forcibly closed after 60 seconds while a search remains active.
findings.fix_hint: Resolve the drain timeout from the active settings at shutdown, applying the environment override afterward. Add an integration test proving a nondefault config value reaches the drain.
source_window: # Defense in depth: a TOML inf cannot unbound the drain. Config value is the default;
# TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env overrides at shutdown; form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling.
shutdown_drain_timeout: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False)
# v2.2: skip Radarr movies without past digital/physical release date
skip_unreleased: bool = True

members.title: New shutdown_drain_timeout field is not read by the shutdown path, so setting it does nothing
members.problem: GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout is added, but the only drain consumer is still the module-level constant _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT in triggarr/search/scheduler.py:81. That constant is set once at import time by _read_shutdown_drain_timeout() (scheduler.py:58-75), which reads only the TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env var, and it is used at scheduler.py:611-656. A grep finds no reference to settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout anywhere. A user who sets this value in config.toml or the UI gets the 60s env default without any warning. The design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-recovery-counts-config-design.md:175) requires a refactor so the value is read from settings at shutdown, and the field comment says the 'config value is the default', but the code does not do that. pending: confirm the scheduler wiring is planned for a later plan in phase 75 before this ships; if this commit ships alone, the setting has no effect.

members.why_it_matters: A visible config field that changes nothing misleads operators, and the drain keeps running at 60s whatever they set.
members.fix_hint: refactor _read_shutdown_drain_timeout to take settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as its default and call it at shutdown time rather than at import

members.title: No upper bound on shutdown_drain_timeout; the comment's 3600.0 form ceiling does not exist in code
members.problem: The field has ge=1.0 but no le. The comment cites a 'form clamp (3600.0)' as the UI ceiling, but a grep finds no such clamp in triggarr/. A hand-edited TOML value such as 1e9 passes validation. That gives a finite but effectively unlimited drain, far above the documented 90s stop_grace_period, so Docker would SIGKILL during the drain. pending: confirm the 3600.0 form clamp lands in a later plan and decide whether the model itself should enforce le=3600.0.

members.title: The new bounded field tightens config validation. Existing configs are unaffected because none of them can contain this key yet
members.problem: The diff adds a field with ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False. A TOML value below 1.0 or a non-finite value now fails validation at load. That is the control doing its job, since the field is new and no deployed config has it. GeneralConfig has no extra='forbid', and the env-var path in scheduler.py stays separate. No supported value is rejected. pending: once the scheduler reads this field, check how a load-time ValidationError is reported (startup abort versus fallback) for an operator who types 0.5.

filtered.title: New shutdown_drain_timeout field is not read by the shutdown path, so setting it does nothing
No upper bound on shutdown_drain_timeout; the comment's 3600.0 form ceiling does not exist in code
The new bounded field tightens config validation. Existing configs are unaffected because none of them can contain this key yet
Env override still accepts inf/nan, so the env var can remove the drain limit that the new config guard blocks
Saving settings in the UI drops shutdown_drain_timeout from the rebuilt general block, so a value set in TOML silently goes back to 60.0
